title: How Europe’s Energy Crisis Exposed Old Fault Lines and New Anxieties

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责报道《纽约时报》每日简讯栏目 DealBook 的商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分精选访谈，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，您可以下载纽约

sentences.en: Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 时报应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，畅享我们所有的新闻报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布里纳·塔弗尼西，这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In the early days of the war in Ukraine, Russia cut off gas supplies to most of Europe, plunging the continent into the most severe energy crisis it had seen in decades.
sentences.zh: 在乌克兰战争的初期，俄罗斯切断了对欧洲大部分地区的天然气供应，使该大陆陷入了数十年来最严重的能源危机。

sentences.en: Today, I talk to my colleague, Matina Steves-Gridneff, about the resulting economic pain and why European leaders are now so afraid of it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了我的同事玛蒂娜·斯特维斯-格里德内夫，探讨由此带来的经济痛苦以及为什么欧洲领导人现在对此如此恐惧。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月25日，星期二。

sentences.en: Matina, hello.
sentences.zh: 玛蒂娜，你好。

sentences.en: Hi, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 嗨，萨布里纳。

sentences.en: Nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Can you describe exactly what's happening right now with energy and energy prices in Europe?
sentences.zh: 你能具体描述一下目前欧洲的能源和能源价格正在发生什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, I guess the simple answer is they're through the roof.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想简单的回答是，它们已经涨上天了。

sentences.en: Time is running out for Europe to contain soaring natural gas prices.
sentences.zh: 欧洲遏制飙升的天然气价格的时间已经不多了。

sentences.en: And because energy just goes into pretty much everything we consume, it's really starting to cause economic chaos.
sentences.zh: 而且因为能源几乎融入了我们消费的每一样东西，它真的开始引发经济混乱了。

sentences.en: Prices are soaring, and major economies like Germany are considering rationing when the cold weather hits.
sentences.zh: 价格正在飙升，而像德国这样的大型经济体正考虑在寒冷天气来临时实施配给制。

sentences.en: When I say energy prices are up, I mean that they're really up by as much as like 500% in some places.
sentences.zh: 当我说能源价格上涨时，我的意思是它们真的涨了很多，在某些地方甚至涨了多达 500%。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常多。

sentences.en: The lights went out early on Friday as one of Paris' most famous landmarks, the Eiffel Tower.
sentences.zh: 周五早些时候，巴黎最著名的地标之一埃菲尔铁塔的灯光提前熄灭了。

sentences.en: The iconic tower shut off its dazzling lights as part of an initiative to save electricity.
sentences.zh: 这座标志性建筑关闭了耀眼的灯光，作为节约电力倡议的一部分。

sentences.en: Across Europe, governments are taking action to switch the lights off in public buildings and even landmarks.
sentences.zh: 在整个欧洲，各国政府都在采取行动，关闭公共建筑甚至地标建筑的灯光。

sentences.en: People are being urged to cut their energy use by showering less and turning off the lights.
sentences.zh: 人们被敦促通过减少洗澡时间和关灯来削减能源消耗。

sentences.en: And there's all sorts of public messaging going on about turning down your heater.
sentences.zh: 关于调低暖气温度的各种公共宣传也在进行中。

sentences.en: They've literally turned down the temperature here at the EU summit buildings.
sentences.zh: 欧盟峰会建筑这里的温度字面意思上已经被调低了。

sentences.en: All EU member states are being asked to make compulsory reductions in their energy consumption.
sentences.zh: 所有欧盟成员国都被要求强制削减能源消耗。

sentences.en: European leaders are passing on the message that we all have to do our bit and just be tougher, so we use less energy.
sentences.zh: 欧洲领导人传递的信息是，我们都必须尽自己的一份力，再坚强一点，从而减少能源使用。

sentences.en: European factories have been shutting down furnaces and keeping production to a minimum.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的工厂一直在关闭熔炉，并将产量保持在最低水平。

sentences.en: With no end in sight for Europe's power problems, could a phase-out of factories be on the cards.
sentences.zh: 随着欧洲的电力问题看不到尽头，淘汰工厂是否也在考虑之中？

sentences.en: So, you see the effects of the energy crisis at the industry level.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以在行业层面看到能源危机的影响。

sentences.en: People across Europe are struggling to pay soaring energy bills.
sentences.zh: 欧洲各地的人们都在艰难地支付飙升的能源账单。

sentences.en: But you also see it on an individual level with bills that have become unaffordable for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以在个人层面看到这一点，账单已经变得让许多人无法承受。

sentences.en: In living memory, it's hard to remember such a sharp rise in energy costs.
sentences.zh: 在有记忆的时期里，很难记起能源成本有过如此急剧的上涨。

sentences.en: It's really a massive burden on European economies right now.
sentences.zh: 这确实是当前欧洲经济的一个巨大负担。

sentences.en: And it's putting everyone under a lot of stress.
sentences.zh: 并且这给每个人都带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: Like, my energy bill here in Belgium has tripled since last year.
sentences.zh: 比如，我在比利时的能源账单自去年以来已经翻了三倍。

sentences.en: I was paying about €240, and now I have to pay more than €700 a month.
sentences.zh: 我以前支付大约 240 欧元，现在每月必须支付超过 700 欧元。

sentences.en: So, it's a big change.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: I mean, we're very fortunate that we can afford it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们非常幸运，我们能够负担得起。

sentences.en: But you can imagine that people with unstable jobs or single-income families or precarious incomes, they can't afford this kind of coSt.
sentences.zh: 但你可以想象，那些工作不稳定、单收入家庭或收入微薄的人，他们负担不起这种成本。

sentences.en: And what's driving all of this?
sentences.zh: 是什么在驱动这一切？

sentences.en: Like, why are energy prices so high right now?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在的能源价格这么高？

sentences.en: I mean, fundamentally, it all goes back to Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the European Union's
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，这一切都可以追溯到俄罗斯对乌克兰的入侵以及欧盟的

sentences.en: decision to support Ukraine and start severing relations with Russia, in particular, wean itself off of Russian energy supplies, such as natural gas.
sentences.zh: 决定：支持乌克兰并开始切断与俄罗斯的关系，特别是摆脱对俄罗斯能源供应（如天然气）的依赖。

sentences.en: That has turned out to be very difficult and very painful.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这非常困难且非常痛苦。

sentences.en: I mean, Europe, as we know, was pretty addicted to Russian energy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，众所周知，欧洲对俄罗斯的能源相当上瘾。

sentences.en: We talked about that on the show before, but remind us exactly sort of how that worked.
sentences.zh: 我们以前在节目中讨论过这一点，但请提醒我们这具体是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: You know, how the war plunged Europe's energy market into so much chaos and created so much pain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，战争是如何将欧洲的能源市场陷入如此大的混乱并制造如此大的痛苦的。

sentences.en: Well, going back to the beginning of the war after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the
sentences.zh: 嗯，回到战争初期，在俄罗斯入侵乌克兰之后，

sentences.en: European Union started hitting Russia with sanctions and also made a pledge for itself, precisely as you said, to start limiting its reliance on Russian energy.
sentences.zh: 欧盟开始对俄罗斯实施制裁，并且正如你所说的那样，对自己做出承诺，开始限制对俄罗斯能源的依赖。

sentences.en: They sort of said, we accept that we've been overly reliant on Russian oil and gas, and we're going to start to do something about this.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上说，我们承认我们对俄罗斯的石油和天然气过度依赖，我们将开始采取行动解决这个问题。

sentences.en: But they didn't even get a chance to really do anything about it because Russia decided to turn off the spigot.
sentences.zh: 但他们甚至没有机会真正采取行动，因为俄罗斯决定关掉水龙头。

sentences.en: Just as an example, European Union imports of Russian natural gas were about 40 percent of the natural gas it imported last year, and this year it's 7 percent at this point.
sentences.zh: 仅举一个例子，欧盟去年进口的俄罗斯天然气约占其进口天然气的 40%，而今年目前这一比例为 7%。

sentences.en: And that's not because the EU did anything, really, other than support Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为欧盟做了什么，实际上除了支持乌克兰之外什么也没做。

sentences.en: It's that the Kremlin decided to punish Europe by sort of weaponizing its gas.
sentences.zh: 而是克里姆林宫决定通过将其天然气武器化来惩罚欧洲。

sentences.en: And that is just a huge change.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: I mean, a massive collapse in something that had been pretty steadfast for many years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个多年来一直相当坚固的事物发生了大规模崩溃。

sentences.en: So what did the EU do?
sentences.zh: 那么欧盟做了什么？

sentences.en: I mean, how did they try to stave off what presumably to them at the time looked like a looming disaster?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们是如何试图避开当时对他们来说似乎即将来临的灾难的？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So this development happened in the warmer months of the year, which was sort of a blessing.
sentences.zh: 所以这一发展发生在一年中较暖和的月份，这算是一种幸运。

sentences.en: But one thing the European Union did across the board was really focus on demand.
sentences.zh: 但欧盟全面采取的一项措施确实是专注于需求。

sentences.en: The one thing they could control, which was how much energy they spent.
sentences.zh: 他们唯一能够控制的东西，那就是他们消耗了多少能源。

sentences.en: But the most immediate things they've done, other than cut demand and trying to save energy, has been buying up lots and lots of natural gas to fill up their storage facilities
sentences.zh: 但除了削减需求和试图节约能源之外，他们采取的最直接的行动就是大量购买天然气，以填满他们的储存设施，

sentences.en: and just make sure they can get through this winter without disruptions.
sentences.zh: 并确保他们能够毫无中断地度过这个冬天。

sentences.en: And already they've hiked the input from Norway and the United States and Algeria,
sentences.zh: 他们已经提高了从挪威、美国和阿尔及利亚的进口，

sentences.en: which are traditional suppliers of natural gas, especially liquefied natural gas, to the European Union.
sentences.zh: 这些国家是欧盟天然气（尤其是液化天然气）的传统供应国。

sentences.en: Some European countries are pursuing deals with sub-Saharan African countries like Mozambique and Senegal.
sentences.zh: 一些欧洲国家正在寻求与莫桑比克和塞内加尔等撒哈拉以南非洲国家达成协议。

sentences.en: They're also looking to the east in places such as Azerbaijan.
sentences.zh: 他们也在向东寻找阿塞拜疆等地方。

sentences.en: And they've done pretty well at that.
sentences.zh: 他们在这方面做得相当不错。

sentences.en: Currently, EU storage facilities are filled up to 90% or more.
sentences.zh: 目前，欧盟的储气设施已填满 90% 或更多。

sentences.en: So they have secured continued electricity production for their countries through this winter, provided this winter is not extraordinarily cold.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要这个冬天不是异常寒冷，他们就确保了国家在整个冬天的持续电力生产。

sentences.en: Okay, so just kind of going back through this here, you have the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以回顾一下这里的过程，就是乌克兰战争。

sentences.en: Russia turns off the spigot.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯关掉了水龙头。

sentences.en: But this is just a massive heart attack in Europe because that's most of Europe's gas.
sentences.zh: 但这就像是欧洲心脏骤停，因为那是欧洲大部分的天然气。

sentences.en: And they go scrambling to solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 然后他们手忙脚乱地解决问题。

sentences.en: And they eventually do solve it by kind of band-aiding together, you know, this new set of supplies.
sentences.zh: 他们最终通过拼凑这套新的供应方案解决了问题。

sentences.en: So problem solved then, right?
sentences.zh: 所以问题解决了吗？

sentences.en: Well, for now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，目前来看是的。

sentences.en: For this winter.
sentences.zh: 为了这个冬天。

sentences.en: Yeah, it made up for the shortfall and they have sufficient electricity's fuel to go through the next few months, certainly until the springtime.
sentences.zh: 是的，它弥补了短缺，他们有足够的电力燃料来度过接下来的几个月，绝对能坚持到春天。

sentences.en: But they were sort of competing against each other and outbidding each other to fill up their natural gas storages.
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上是在互相竞争、竞相出价来填满他们的天然气储量。

sentences.en: They being all these European countries.
sentences.zh: 他们指的是所有这些欧洲国家。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that sends an already very, very high price even higher.
sentences.zh: 这使得原本已经非常非常高的价格变得更高。

sentences.en: And Germany is really being singled out as a prime offender in this because they had the most reliance on Russian gas.
sentences.zh: 德国真的被当作主要罪魁祸首被点名批评，因为他们对俄罗斯天然气的依赖最大。

sentences.en: But they're also the richeSt.
sentences.zh: 但他们也是最富有的。

sentences.en: So they didn't really sort of stop and wait to look at what the price was, whatever the price was,
sentences.zh: 所以他们并没有真正停下来等待看价格是多少，无论价格是多少，

sentences.en: they were willing to pay it so long as they could fill up their natural gas storage facilities.
sentences.zh: 只要能填满他们的天然气储气设施，他们就愿意支付。

sentences.en: And that did lead them to create problems for smaller and poorer European Union countries that couldn't afford the prices at the level that they were being set.
sentences.zh: 这确实给无力承担当时设定价格的欧盟较小和较贫穷国家带来了麻烦。

sentences.en: So, you know, yes, the good news is that for the European Union countries, the scrambling worked.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，是的，好消息是对于欧盟国家来说，这种争夺起作用了。

sentences.en: Cutting demand, buying up whatever they could, filling up those storage facilities and looking for alternative sources, all of that has been working.
sentences.zh: 削减需求、竭尽全力购买、填满储气设施并寻找替代来源，所有这些都在起作用。

sentences.en: But the bad news is that it's come at a huge uptick in energy prices.
sentences.zh: 但坏消息是，代价是能源价格的大幅飙升。

sentences.en: And that started to expose divisions among EU countries because they were bidding against each other, like kind of acting at cross purposes.
sentences.zh: 这开始暴露出欧盟国家之间的分歧，因为它们互相竞标，有点像在各行其是。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: They didn't do it together.
sentences.zh: 它们没有齐心协力。

sentences.en: And the divisions are exactly what Russia revels in.
sentences.zh: 而这些分歧正是俄罗斯所乐见其成的。

sentences.en: Putin basically celebrates the European front, which is trying to stick together despite economic adversity to support Ukraine, splintering.
sentences.zh: 普京基本上是在庆贺欧洲阵线的分裂，这个阵线原本正试图不顾经济逆境团结一致支持乌克兰。

sentences.en: He went on an economics and business conference recently and was sort of quite sort of sarcastic about it.
sentences.zh: 他最近出席了一个经济和商业会议，对此表现得相当讽刺。

sentences.en: Oh, are you struggling over there?
sentences.zh: 哦，你们那边遇到困难了吗？

sentences.en: Well, you say the word and I'll turn the spigot back on.
sentences.zh: 行啊，只要你们说句话，我就把阀门重新打开。

sentences.en: And of course, on Russian media, there's all these stories about how people in the European Union are really struggling,
sentences.zh: 当然，在俄罗斯媒体上，有各种关于欧盟人民如何陷入挣扎的报道，

sentences.en: that EU sanctions are hurting Europeans more than they're hurting Russians.
sentences.zh: 声称欧盟的制裁对欧洲人造成的伤害大于对俄罗斯人的伤害。

sentences.en: So you can see that this is something that really plays into the Russian playbook.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，这完全迎合了俄罗斯的剧本。

sentences.en: They want to see an exhaustion of the support for Ukraine, a fatigue with the war, and especially a fatigue with paying the economic costs of supporting Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他们希望看到对乌克兰支持的耗尽、对战争的疲劳，尤其是对支付支持乌克兰的经济成本的疲劳。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Putin is basically waiting for Europe to get tired of the situation,
sentences.zh: 普京基本上在等待欧洲对这种局势感到厌倦，

sentences.en: get tired of this war and want to go back to their own economies and back to their own problems and stop supporting Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 对这场战争感到厌倦，并想要回到他们自己的经济和问题中去，停止支持乌克兰。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in a way, it's not a crazy thought.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这并非疯狂的想法。

sentences.en: These super high energy costs are building into growing prices for goods, fueling record inflation around the European Union.
sentences.zh: 这些超高的能源成本正在推高商品价格，助长了整个欧盟创纪录的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Inflation in the EU is around 10, 11 percent.
sentences.zh: 欧盟的通货膨胀率在 10% 到 11% 左右。

sentences.en: Where I am in Belgium, it's 12 percent, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我所在的比利时，这一数字是 12%。

sentences.en: Wow, 12 percent.
So it's significantly higher than what you guys have in the U.S., which is already pretty high, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它明显高于你们美国的水平，美国已经相当高了，对吧？

sentences.en: I think inflation in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想美国的通货膨胀率

sentences.en: is 8 percent.
And so where does that leave European leaders?
sentences.zh: 那么这给欧洲领导人留下了什么局面？

sentences.en: I think European leaders realize that we're at a tipping point where things are about to get a lot worse.
sentences.zh: 我认为欧洲领导人意识到我们正处于一个临界点，事情即将变得更加糟糕。

sentences.en: Maybe the sort of total nightmare scenario of like widespread power outages in Europe has been averted.
sentences.zh: 也许欧洲大面积断电的那种全面噩梦般的场景已经被避免了。

sentences.en: But the price of fixing that problem has been huge.
sentences.zh: 但解决这个问题的代价是巨大的。

sentences.en: And they're also starting to worry about their own governments, their own political survival.
sentences.zh: 他们也开始担心他们自己的政府，他们自己的政治生存。

sentences.en: And why would they worry about that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要担心这个？

sentences.en: I mean, maybe that seems like a dumb question, but how does this relate to that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来可能是一个愚蠢的问题，但这与此有什么关系？

sentences.en: Well, it isn't a dumb question at all, because when economic pain becomes this acute,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这一点也不愚蠢，因为当经济痛苦变得如此剧烈时，

sentences.en: when you have a real cost of living crisis that affects multiple layers of society and industry, people respond in unpredictable ways.
sentences.zh: 当你面临一场真正影响到社会和行业多个层面的生活成本危机时，人们的反应是无法预测的。

sentences.en: It becomes a major problem for politicians, especially if they don't have good policies in place to to deal with the problem.
sentences.zh: 这成为政客们的一个重大问题，特别是如果他们没有制定好的政策来应对这个问题的话。

sentences.en: And you see the impact of that on the street, in polling numbers.
sentences.zh: 你可以在街头和民意调查数据中看到这种影响。

sentences.en: It becomes a threat to the sustainability of governments.
sentences.zh: 这成了对政府可持续性的威胁。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Mattina, how much are we actually starting to see political upheaval in Europe because of these rising energy prices?
sentences.zh: 马蒂娜，因为这些不断上涨的能源价格，我们在欧洲真正开始看到多少政治动荡？

sentences.en: Well, Sabrina, I do think it's starting to bubble.
sentences.zh: 嗯，萨布里纳，我确实认为它开始酝酿了。

sentences.en: Most European nations are facing sharply rising inflation.
sentences.zh: 大多数欧洲国家都面临着急剧上升的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: The latest IMF data presents a grim picture.
sentences.zh: 国际货币基金组织（IMF）的最新数据呈现了一幅严峻的图景。

sentences.en: I mean, across Europe over the last several weeks, we're seeing demonstrations with thousands of people taking to the streets.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在过去的几周里，整个欧洲都能看到成千上万的人走上街头的游行示威。

sentences.en: More than 100,000 people nationwide answered a call from left-wing parties.
sentences.zh: 全国有超过 10 万人响应了左翼政党的号召。

sentences.en: In France, for example, some of the major labor unions there organized a march in Paris last week to demand wage increases and higher benefits.
sentences.zh: 例如在法国，一些主要的工会在上周组织了巴黎游行，要求增加工资和提高福利。

sentences.en: In the city of Nantes, hospital staff, social educators, students and workers from other sectors are also demonstrating.
sentences.zh: 在南特市，医院员工、社会教育工作者、学生以及其他行业的工人也在举行示威活动。

sentences.en: Or in Germany.
sentences.zh: 或者在德国。

sentences.en: We're no longer up to our necks in water.
sentences.zh: 我们不再是没顶之灾了。

sentences.en: We're in the process of thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们正在思考中。

sentences.en: We can't go on.
sentences.zh: 我们再也撑不下去了。

sentences.en: We need help.
sentences.zh: 我们需要帮助。

sentences.en: Protesters rallied there as well, decrying rising energy prices and living expenses.
sentences.zh: 那里也有抗议者集会，谴责不断上涨的能源价格和生活开支。

sentences.en: And in a really interesting example.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的例子。

sentences.en: Under the banner of Czech Republic FirSt.
sentences.zh: 打着“捷克共和国第一”的旗号。

sentences.en: In the Czech Republic, 70,000 people last month came out to voice their opposition to the European Union and NATO.
sentences.zh: 在捷克共和国，上个月有七万人走上街头，表达他们对欧盟和北约的反对。

sentences.en: They called for the ending of sanctions against Russia and to instead establish a new gas supply deal.
sentences.zh: 他们呼吁停止对俄罗斯的制裁，转而建立新的天然气供应协议。

sentences.en: Protesters also saying that the Czech Republic should be militarily neutral.
sentences.zh: 抗议者还表示，捷克共和国应该保持军事中立。

sentences.en: And there, they linked their economic problems directly to the EU sanctions against Russia and EU support for Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他们将经济问题直接归咎于欧盟对俄罗斯的制裁以及欧盟对乌克兰的支持。

sentences.en: So I think what's important to note here is that the cost of living crisis that we're living through right now is worse than what we've had in a really, really long time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这里值得注意的是，我们当前经历的生活成本危机，比我们很长很长一段时间以来经历的都要严重。

sentences.en: And that kind of economic pain can have political consequences.
sentences.zh: 这种经济阵痛可能会带来政治后果。

sentences.en: What do you mean political consequences?
sentences.zh: 你所说的政治后果是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, the majority of people are simply demanding better policies from their governments to help them weather the cost of living crisis that is now out of control.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大多数人只是要求政府出台更好的政策，来帮助他们度过目前已经失控的生活成本危机。

sentences.en: But take the Czech Republic.
sentences.zh: 但以捷克共和国为例。

sentences.en: Those big protests we saw there, they were being agitated to a certain extent and certainly sort of taken advantage off by fringe groups on the far right.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里看到的大规模抗议活动，在某种程度上受到了极右翼边缘团体的煽动，他们当然也借机加以利用。

sentences.en: And we're certainly seeing it also on the far left that are finding an opportunity in this cost of living crisis to basically parrot Russian propaganda, saying, for example, that,
sentences.zh: 我们当然也看到极左翼群体也在利用这场生活成本危机的机会，基本上在鹦鹉学舌般地散布俄罗斯宣传，比如说，

sentences.en: you know, the EU has sanctioned Russian gas, which is not true.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，欧盟制裁了俄罗斯天然气，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: It's Russia that chose to turn off the tap and cut gas supplies to Europe.
sentences.zh: 是俄罗斯选择关闭阀门，切断对欧洲的天然气供应。

sentences.en: But sanctions have so far quite explicitly exempted Russian gas precisely because European Union countries need it so much.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，制裁明确排除了俄罗斯天然气，正是因为欧盟国家对它的需求太大了。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, what those fringe groups are arguing is that what's to blame for the cost of living crisis is basically Europe's support of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上讲，这些边缘团体争辩说，造成生活成本危机的罪魁祸首基本上是欧洲对乌克兰的支持。

sentences.en: If Europe would just sort of capitulate to Russia's advance in Ukraine and its invasion, things wouldn't be this bad.
sentences.zh: 如果欧洲只是向俄罗斯在乌克兰的推进及其入侵妥协投降，事情就不会这么糟了。

sentences.en: So it's not just sort of an abstract thing they're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是他们谈论的某种抽象的事情。

sentences.en: It's a real fear.
sentences.zh: 这是一种真实的恐惧。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: that this economic anxiety could inject a lot of uncertainty into their political systems and be fodder for fringe and extreme parties who are trying to make arguments against them.
sentences.zh: 这种经济焦虑可能会给他们的政治体制注入大量的不确定性，并成为边缘和极端政党反对他们的弹药。

sentences.en: I mean, that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对正确。

sentences.en: In recent European history, we have seen a pretty direct link between economic anxiety and crises and openings for populism, especially from the right,
sentences.zh: 在欧洲近代史上，我们看到经济焦虑和危机与民粹主义（尤其是来自右翼的民粹主义）的机遇之间存在着相当直接的联系，

sentences.en: but also occasionally from the left.
sentences.zh: 但偶尔也来自左翼。

sentences.en: For example, we saw this at the back of the Eurozone crisis and Greece's crisis in 2011 to 2015.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们在2011年至2015年的欧元区危机和希腊危机之后看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Then we saw it after that in the Yellow Vest movement in France.
sentences.zh: 然后我们在法国的“黄马甲”运动中再次看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And with every crisis, these movements and these parties just gain a little more popularity.
sentences.zh: 随着每一次危机，这些运动和这些政党就会获得多一点的支持率。

sentences.en: They gain bigger audiences.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了更多的受众。

sentences.en: And I think that history is front and center as EU leaders try to sort of form some kind of consensus and stay away of people's frustrations that's snowballing toward them to bring down the cost of living,
sentences.zh: 我认为，当欧盟领导人试图达成某种共识，以避开向他们滚雪球般涌来的民众的不满情绪以降低生活成本时，这段历史就摆在最显眼的位置，

sentences.en: but also to sort of take this fuel away from populist parties.
sentences.zh: 同时也是为了剥夺民粹主义政党的这种燃料。

sentences.en: So what are these leaders then doing to avert that?
sentences.zh: 那么这些领导人为避免这种情况正在做些什么呢？

sentences.en: How are they taking action?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何采取行动的？

sentences.en: Well, so far, they've thrown money at the problem, like a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，到目前为止，他们一直在向问题砸钱，砸了大量的钱。

sentences.en: Hundreds of billions of euros in subsidies, nationalizing energy companies, spending a lot of cash out of their budgets in order to try and support households and businesses.
sentences.zh: 数千亿欧元的补贴，将能源公司国有化，从预算中支出大量现金，以试图支持家庭和企业。

sentences.en: These policies are not sustainable, not least because they're extremely, extremely expensive.
sentences.zh: 这些政策是不可持续的，不仅因为它们极其极其昂贵。

sentences.en: So they need to do something a bit more fundamental to break this loop of energy prices.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们需要采取更根本的措施来打破这个能源价格的循环。

sentences.en: They know that they have to agree on some stronger measures than just buying up all the gas they can find and just spending huge sums of money subsidizing people's bills.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，他们必须达成比买下所有能找到的天然气、花费巨资补贴人们账单更强有力的措施。

sentences.en: Just last week, EU leaders met here in Brussels to put in place some of those bigger measures,
sentences.zh: 就在上周，欧盟领导人在布鲁塞尔会晤，以实施其中一些更大的措施，

sentences.en: like buying up gas together for the next winter and even capping the price they're prepared to pay for natural gas.
sentences.zh: 比如在今年冬天联合购买天然气，甚至对他们准备支付的天然气价格设定上限。

sentences.en: And the clock's ticking because some countries face elections next year and they're trying to outrun this problem so they don't enter these elections on a really bad economic situation.
sentences.zh: 时间在流逝，因为一些国家明年将面临选举，他们正试图跑赢这个问题，以免带着非常糟糕的经济形势进入这些选举。

sentences.en: And I think European leaders are really motivated to keep a united front supporting Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我认为欧洲领导人非常有动力保持支持乌克兰的统一阵线。

sentences.en: But to do that, they've got to keep their people behind them.
sentences.zh: 但要做到这一点，他们必须让民众坚定支持他们。

sentences.en: I mean, at some point, self-preservation presumably kicks in, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某个时刻，自我保护本能大概会发挥作用，对吧？

sentences.en: And for some Europeans, it's becoming a real question about why their governments are continuing to support Ukraine in this very expensive war.
sentences.zh: 对于一些欧洲人来说，这成了一个真正的问题：为什么他们的政府要在这个代价高昂的战争中继续支持乌克兰。

sentences.en: Well, I guess that's ultimately the question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这最终是那个问题。

sentences.en: And to be fair, European public opinion seems to largely be supportive of staying behind Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，欧洲的公众舆论似乎在很大程度上支持坚定支持乌克兰。

sentences.en: For example, polling in Germany last month showed that 70 percent of the population is still in favor of strongly supporting Ukraine despite higher energy prices.
sentences.zh: 例如，德国上个月的民调显示，尽管能源价格上涨，但仍有70%的人口赞成大力支持乌克兰。

sentences.en: But the truth is, the longer this problem festers, and unless European leaders get some strong policies in place, the more this kind of support for Ukraine will wane,
sentences.zh: 但事实是，这个问题发酵的时间越长，除非欧洲领导人制定出强有力的政策，否则这种对乌克兰的支持就会越发减弱，

sentences.en: in particular in countries that are maybe poorer or have closer traditional ties to Russia.
sentences.zh: 特别是在那些可能较贫穷或与俄罗斯有更紧密传统联系的国家。

sentences.en: And as the costs rise, you can't count on people's resilience and support forever.
sentences.zh: 随着成本上升，你不能永远指望人们的韧性和支持。

sentences.en: Matina, thank you.
sentences.zh: 玛蒂娜，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: I am humbled and honored to have the support of my parliamentary colleagues and to be elected as leader of the Conservative and Unionist Party.
sentences.zh: 我很荣幸并深感谦卑地获得议会同僚的支持，并当选为保守党和统一党领袖。

sentences.en: Rishi Sunak will become Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after prevailing in a chaotic race for Britain's Conservative Party leadership.
sentences.zh: 在经历了英国保守党领袖之位的一场混乱竞选后，里希·苏纳克将成为英国首相。

sentences.en: Sunak, who is 42 and the son of Indian immigrants, will be Britain's third leader in seven weeks and is the first Prime Minister of Colour in British history.
sentences.zh: 现年42岁的苏纳克是印度移民的儿子，他将成为英国七周内的第三位领导人，也是英国历史上第一位有色人种首相。

sentences.en: The United Kingdom is a great country, but there is no doubt we face a profound economic challenge.
sentences.zh: 英国是一个伟大的国家，但毫无疑问，我们面临着严峻的经济挑战。

sentences.en: He replaces Liz Truss, who resigned under pressure last week after her economic agenda caused turmoil.
sentences.zh: 他接替了伊丽莎白·特拉斯，后者在她的经济议程引发动荡后于上周在压力下辞职。

sentences.en: We now need stability and unity, and I will make it my utmost priority to bring our party and our country together.
sentences.zh: 我们现在需要稳定和团结，我将把凝聚我们党和我们的国家作为我的最高优先事项。

sentences.en: Sunak now faces soaring inflation, but also steep hurdles in unifying his own party.
sentences.zh: 苏纳克现在面临着飙升的通货膨胀，以及在统一自己党派方面的巨大障碍。

sentences.en: The Conservatives lag behind the opposition Labour Party by more than 30 percentage points in the polls.
sentences.zh: 保守党在民调中落后反对党工党30个百分点以上。

sentences.en: And, U.S.
sentences.zh: 另外，根据一项权威的国家考试，

sentences.en: students experienced major setbacks in both math and reading during the COVID pandemic, according to an authoritative national exam.
sentences.zh: 美国学生在新冠大流行期间，在数学和阅读方面都经历了重大挫折。

sentences.en: The declines happened in nearly every state and across almost all demographic groups.
sentences.zh: 这种下降几乎发生在每一个州以及几乎所有人口统计群体中。

sentences.en: The results were particularly devastating in math.
sentences.zh: 数学方面的结果尤其具有毁灭性。

sentences.en: Just 26% of 8th graders were proficient, down from 34% in 2019.
sentences.zh: 只有26%的八年级学生达到熟练水平，低于2019年的34%。

sentences.en: It was the steepest drop since the test was first administered in the early 1990s.
sentences.zh: 这是自20世纪90年代初首次进行该测试以来最大幅度的下降。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Muv Zadie and Diana Wynn.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由穆夫·扎迪和戴安娜·温制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George, with help from Patricia Willens.
sentences.zh: 由马克·乔治编辑，帕特里夏·威伦斯协助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell, Marion Lozano, and Rowan Demisto, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔、马里恩·洛萨诺和罗文·德米斯托的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《今日每日》节目的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: We'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又扣人心弦的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格一起，讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
